steps: Find the two multiples of 10 closest to 40: 40 and 50.
40 is 0 away from 40 and 10 away from 50.
The nearer multiple of 10 is 40, so that is the rounded value. (A distance exactly halfway rounds up.)
The nearest multiples of 100 are 600 and 700.
647 is 47 away from 600 and 53 away from 700.
600 is nearer, so 647 rounds to 600.

commonErrors.likelyCause: Rounded toward the wrong neighboring multiple, or rounded down out of habit regardless of distance.
commonErrors.remediation: Have the learner mark both neighboring multiples on a number line and measure the distance to each before choosing.

scoringGuidance: Score the stated target for locating three-digit numbers on an open number line: accuracy, the quality of the model or reasoning, and the revision. Accept any valid approach that meets the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.
masteryRule: One correct response cannot establish mastery of locating three-digit numbers on an open number line. Mastery requires accurate independent evidence plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, separated by time or by representation. Guided success is recorded as supported and is not weighted as independent evidence.
remediationGuidance: round-to-nearest-ten-or-hundred (3.NBT.1): if the learner misses these, reteach with the worked example “Round 647 to the nearest 100.” and require the reasoning for each step before another attempt.
extensionGuidance: Apply locating three-digit numbers on an open number line under a new constraint, compare two strategies and justify which is more efficient, or write an original problem and its worked solution. The learner may not complete another learner's graded work.
